# Stock Management

Next.js application for Orders, Shipments, inventory/movements, Sales, expenses and HR, using Supabase, Google Sheets/Drive, LINE and Loyverse. The scoped modular refactor is complete through [PR #40](https://github.com/volkswg/stock-management/pull/40): active code uses canonical feature, infrastructure and composition owners; `src/externals/` is removed. Some other compatibility paths remain intentionally supported.

**Production safety:** completion of the refactor does not certify authentication, authorization, live provider behavior or concurrent writes. [Issue #38](https://github.com/volkswg/stock-management/issues/38) tracks access-control verification, CI and isolated smoke tests. Check access restrictions before exposing employee/payroll or write-capable APIs; do not run mutating smoke tests against production.

Production uses Supabase. Storage cleanup is complete through PR81: operational sidecars are removed, 47 lifecycle fields are native timestamps, and validation uses 23 CHECK constraints plus one shared guard (52 operational functions). Browser writes and LINE are open. The app remains on PR80 source `31af820`; PR81 was database-only. See [production operations](docs/database-migration.md#current-production) and [release evidence](docs/refactoring/progress.md#latest-production-release).

## Start here

- [Architecture guide](docs/architecture/README.md) for current ownership and documentation navigation; [engineering rules](AGENTS.md) for safe development.
- [Roadmap](docs/refactoring/roadmap.md) for **current and next work**; [progress ledger](docs/refactoring/progress.md) for completed PRs and archived evidence; [verification](docs/refactoring/verification.md) for safe commands and limits.
- Operational guides: [expenses](docs/expenses.md), [movement migration](docs/movement-migration.md), [LINE rich-menu links](docs/rich-menu-links.md) and [stock adjustments](docs/shop-stock-adjustments.md).

## Local development

Use Node 24 (verified 24.22.1) and the repository's existing dependencies and yarn.lock. Run `npm run dev`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Source is under `src/`; Next routes are in `src/app`. Use approved development configuration. Architecture verification uses isolated copies without application credentials; do not start live integrations or run operational setup as a check.

## Google Sheets worksheet names

`GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` is required for the workbook. The 23 `GOOGLE_SHEETS_*_WORKSHEET_NAME` settings are **optional**: `src/config/index.ts` supplies the existing worksheet-tab defaults, including `orders`, `shipments`, `movements` and `movement_details`. The `.env.example` template omits these redundant overrides.

Keep or add a worksheet-name environment variable **only if** its actual workbook tab differs from the default. For example, to use a tab named `shop_orders` instead of `orders`, set `GOOGLE_SHEETS_ORDERS_WORKSHEET_NAME=shop_orders`. Before deleting overrides from an existing environment (local or deployment settings), verify every actual tab matches the corresponding default. Changing the template does not change deployed environment variables or rename any Google Sheets tabs.

## Loyverse Configuration

`LOYVERSE_ACCOUNT_SOURCE=env|sheet` selects the server-only account source. Unset or blank defaults to **env**; unknown values fail validation. Existing JSON configuration remains supported, with the same array order, IDs and optional store filter:

```dotenv
LOYVERSE_ACCOUNT_SOURCE=env
LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_JSON=[{"id":"main-shop","shopName":"Main Shop","accessToken":"...","storeId":"optional-store-id"}]
```

Keep credentials in approved private configuration, never source control, screenshots, chat, logs or `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables. There is no credential editing page or management endpoint. Existing account/shop APIs return only their existing public metadata.

### Prepare the account worksheet in the existing workbook

These are **owner actions after review**, not steps performed by this PR:

1. Use the existing `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` workbook. Sheet mode always reads that workbook; there is no account-specific spreadsheet ID or workbook fallback. Use a dedicated `loyverse_accounts` tab, never the existing `shops` tab.
2. **Every workbook reader can see the access-token cells. Hiding or protecting a worksheet does not provide separate read access.** Restrict and audit sharing before adding tokens. Keep access limited to the owner, required service account and only people explicitly trusted with credentials; remove broad/inherited/link sharing. If access cannot be restricted appropriately, keep env mode until it can. Keep the service account's existing operational permissions needed for business writes; do not downgrade them. The account reader still requests the read-only Sheets scope and never creates tabs, repairs headers or writes credentials.
3. In that existing workbook, create one worksheet named exactly `loyverse_accounts`. Put these six case-sensitive headers in A1:F1, in this order:

   ```text
   id,shopName,storeId,accessToken,active,sortOrder
   ```

   | Column | Value |
   | --- | --- |
   | id | Original `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_JSON` account `id`, unchanged and unique across all rows |
   | shopName | Original display name |
   | storeId | Original store ID, or blank if absent; blank retains the existing unrestricted store behavior |
   | accessToken | Original private token; required for active accounts, may be blank for disabled accounts |
   | active | TRUE/FALSE (checkboxes or those case-insensitive text values) |
   | sortOrder | Unique nonnegative safe integer, including disabled rows; no ties, fractions or thousands separators |

4. Format A:D as **plain text** before manual copying, so IDs, store IDs and tokens retain leading zeros and exact text. Use ungrouped integer formatting for F. Privately copy each existing JSON account to a row, set active to TRUE and assign sortOrder in the **original JSON array order**, for example 10, 20, 30. Never generate replacement IDs or substitute `shops.id` or `storeId` for the existing account ID. Do not modify the operational shops, receipt, payroll or stock worksheets.
5. Compare the copied IDs, names, optional store IDs, token values and ordering privately with the existing configuration. Do not export that comparison into issue/PR attachments or logs. Existing values are trimmed as in env mode. Duplicate IDs/order values, malformed flags, missing enabled tokens, bad headers and a header-only/empty worksheet fail closed; fully empty rows are ignored. An all-disabled valid worksheet returns an empty active list.

The application sorts enabled accounts by sortOrder and uses the first as the existing default. Disabled accounts cannot be selected for provider reads/sync or new account mappings. Their stored financial history is preserved: combined reports and existing Shop Master mappings may still include historical records. Existing mappings remain editable even when an account is disabled or removed. Disabling does not revoke a provider token or cancel a request already in flight.

### Enable, verify and roll back on Vercel

1. Keep `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_JSON` unchanged for rollback. In the project's **Settings → Environment Variables**, choose only the intended environment/branch. Set the source to sheet using the already configured operational workbook:

   ```dotenv
   LOYVERSE_ACCOUNT_SOURCE=sheet
   # Existing setting; this is also the account workbook.
   GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID=<existing workbook ID>
   ```

   `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID` is the only workbook setting. The former `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_SPREADSHEET_ID` setting is no longer read, even if an old deployment setting remains. If upgrading from a separate account workbook, manually copy the six-column tab into the existing workbook and verify IDs/order privately before switching to this code. No copying or Vercel setting changes are performed by this PR. Keep the existing service-account settings. Scope staging/preview to its own restricted test workbook and credentials, not production data. Never use `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefixes.
2. After owner-approved deployment of the reviewed code, verify in an isolated staging environment first. Env changes apply to new deployments; changing the dashboard setting alone does not switch a running deployment. Sheet mode never evaluates the JSON account source. A missing/invalid `GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID`, bad rows, a missing tab, denied access or provider failure produces a safe error. There is no alternate workbook or env/JSON fallback.
3. Check `/api/loyverse/accounts` returns only the expected active `id`/`shopName` pairs in the original order. Verify the default and explicitly selected account, optional store filtering, daily/dashboard/profit totals, sync-status lists, Inventory and attendance shop lists, and Expenses Shop Master account mappings. Inspect response keys and logs for confidentiality without copying tokens into them. Metadata requests must not return tokens, store credentials or raw Google errors.
4. Using staging fixtures, check a disabled account is absent and cannot be newly selected, an existing disabled-account Shop Master mapping can still be edited, and missing workbook access produces a safe failure. Verify Sales sync on an approved unsynced past date and its repeat/idempotency behavior; do not run test sync writes against production. Private accounts are read once per lookup without a cross-request cache or new retry policy; workbook outages therefore block affected lookups.
5. Roll back by setting `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNT_SOURCE=env` and deploying a new owner-approved deployment with the retained, valid `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_JSON`. Verify IDs/order and normal operation again. There are no business-data migrations to undo; the account worksheet is simply unused in env mode.

Delete the deployed `LOYVERSE_ACCOUNTS_JSON` value **only after** successful owner verification, completion of the agreed rollback window, confirmation that every environment/deployment that needs it has migrated, and an approved secure recovery plan. Older deployments or an env-mode rollback still need it. Removing the variable is a separate owner operation; this PR retains JSON support and does not delete credentials, migrate production records or deploy anything. Live sharing, access and account correctness remain owner verification steps.

## Movement creation mode

Set `MOVEMENT_CREATE_MODE` in the deployment environment, then redeploy:

- `quantity_photo` (default, including when unset): existing LINE journey —
  choose NJ/YY, enter quantity/breakdown, send photo, then repeat or close the bag.
- `photo_only`: choose NJ/YY, send product photos, then Close Bag → Another Shop
  or Summary. Forwarded text is not used as a quantity/note. Each photo is saved
  with an unset quantity; enter the note/quantity on the movement detail web page.
  Notes such as `ดำ 5` or `5` calculate quantity 5 and remain saved as entered.

The switch is global; LINE does not show a mode selector. Resumed sessions use
whichever mode the deployed environment selects. Existing saved items are not
converted. Delivery requires a positive quantity for every item in either mode.
Photo-only items use the LINE image message ID, so different images do not share
an item cursor and re-delivery of an already-saved image reuses its item.
This is not a distributed webhook queue; cross-request command ordering still
requires durable per-user serialization if strict ordering is needed.

## Salary advances and payroll settlement

Open **Human resources → Salary advances** (`/employees/advances`). This is a
shop-owner payment ledger, not an employee request/approval workflow.

1. **Record advance** after handing over/transferring money to an employee. Choose
   an active employee and shop, enter the actual amount paid, payment date,
   first payroll month to deduct from, optional reference and note, then
   **Save advance**. The entry is immediately paid and included in payroll;
   there is no separate request, approval or payment-confirmation stage.
   Paid advances cannot be edited, cancelled or deleted through the app.
2. In **Payroll**, review gross earnings, advance deductions, net salary and
   balance carried forward. Expand details or export the salary PDF for the
   individual payments and deductions. Deductions are oldest-first and capped
   at earnings, so net salary is never negative. Excess advances roll forward.
3. Pay the remaining salary, then **Settle payroll** with the final payment date
   and optional reference. This saves an immutable calculation snapshot and
   recovers only that month's allocated deduction. Merely viewing/exporting
   payroll does not recover an advance. Zero-net payroll can also be settled.

Existing unpaid records from the earlier workflow remain **Not paid** and never
become deductions automatically. The owner can **Record payment** directly,
without approval, or **Remove unpaid entry** to retain its cancelled history.
The API rejects the former approval action and cannot create new unpaid entries.
The worksheet layout is preserved: old `requestedDate` and `requestedAmount`
columns are compatibility metadata, set to the payment date and actual paid
amount on new records. No migration or rewriting of existing history is needed.

Example: ฿15,000 base + ฿2,000 commission − ฿3,000 advance − ฿2,000 advance =
฿12,000 remaining salary. The salary cost is ฿17,000, not ฿22,000.
These actions do **not** create expense entries; maintain the existing salary
expense separately and do not count advance payments again as extra salary cost.

Settlements are final in this version (no reopen/undo interface). Settle an
employee's months in chronological order. Once a month or later month is settled,
new advances/advance payments cannot be backdated into it. Older unpaid entries in
locked periods can still be removed and paid advances recorded in an open month. Salary or
attendance edits do not rewrite settled payroll. An employee with a paid advance
balance remains visible in payroll even without attendance; dates outside their
employment do not generate a new monthly base salary.

Two worksheets are added lazily on the first corresponding write, preserving
other sheets. Reads alone do not initialize these worksheets. Optional overrides:

- `GOOGLE_SHEETS_EMPLOYEE_ADVANCES_WORKSHEET_NAME` (default `employee_advances`)
- `GOOGLE_SHEETS_PAYROLL_SETTLEMENTS_WORKSHEET_NAME` (default `payroll_settlements`)

The service account needs permission to add worksheets. Unexpected existing
headers cause an error instead of being overwritten. Financial rows use RAW
cell input to preserve dates, references, notes and JSON snapshots literally.
A settlement and all its recovery allocations are stored in one row, avoiding
partial writes across the advance and settlement sheets. Creation identifiers,
state timestamps and payroll revisions protect ordinary retries/stale forms;
identical settlement retries return the existing settlement. Google Sheets has
no cross-instance transactions: process payroll/advance changes one operator at
a time rather than concurrently from multiple sessions. Do not manually alter
paid advances or settlement snapshots in Sheets.

## Shop stock adjustments

Record employee gifts, damage, samples, personal use, returns and corrections in
**Monthly stock count → Stock adjustments**. Entries update only the selected
shop/month; physical counts and finances remain separate. Corrections retain
history using reversals and linked replacements. See
[the stock-adjustment workflow](docs/shop-stock-adjustments.md) for calculations,
Loyverse duplicate prevention, warnings, optional photo links and worksheet setup.

# Architecture guide

## Current system

Orders, Shipments, Inventory, Sales, Expenses, HR and LINE own their business
workflows. Shared infrastructure owns provider transports and PostgreSQL sessions;
composition wires feature-owned ports. `src/externals/` and `src/features/` are
retired. Supported service/script compatibility remains explicit.

Production uses Supabase with stable IDs, named-column authority and 47 native
business lifecycle timestamps. The operational cell/ordinal/kind/lexeme sidecars are gone.
PR81's database-only release consolidated validators and added timestamp CHECKs;
PR84 subsequently added the eleven-column media catalog and five references; there
are 60 operational functions and 52 operational triggers after PR85's five duplicate
media URL columns were retired. Browser writes and LINE reopened after reconciliation.
PR83 added scoped Order/Movement edit tokens; current production is PR85 `80db4ae`.
Consolidating `archived_at` into `deletedAt` is prepared local/PR work and has not
changed production. [The release gate](../database-migration.md#deletedat-soft-delete-consolidation-prepared-production-unchanged)
keeps old and new layouts compatible until separately approved maintenance.
Old business Sheets are read-only; Drive and private integration-account ownership
are unchanged. See [production operations](../database-migration.md) and the
[latest release evidence](../refactoring/progress.md#latest-production-release).

New staff authentication/RBAC/shop permissions and backup automation remain deferred.
Existing access controls are preserved; migration completion is not an access-
control certification. Future live changes require their own approval.

## Find the right document

| Question | Authoritative source |
| --- | --- |
| Where do files belong and which dependencies are allowed? | [Architecture rules](rules.md) |
| Who owns current modules, worksheets and compatibility paths? | [Ownership map](migration-map.md) |
| Which observable contracts must remain stable? | [Architecture decisions](decisions.md) |
| How is production stored, recovered and maintained? | [Supabase operations](../database-migration.md) |
| What is the next authorized scope? | [Roadmap](../refactoring/roadmap.md) |
| Which PR/CI/release proves a result? Where is older evidence? | [Evidence ledger](../refactoring/progress.md) |
| How are local/CI checks run safely? | [Verification guide](../refactoring/verification.md) |
| How should work be prepared and reviewed? | [Engineering rules](../../AGENTS.md) |
| What is planned for staff access? | [Authentication roadmap](user-authentication-roadmap.md) |

## Feature guides

[Expenses](../expenses.md), [movements](../movement-migration.md),
[stock adjustments](../shop-stock-adjustments.md) and
[LINE menu links](../rich-menu-links.md) keep their established paths. Their feature
workflows and optional Sheets-backend instructions are separate from current
production storage and do not authorize provider or production mutations.

## Documentation ownership

Maintain current ownership here and in the map, implementation rules in one guide,
operations in one runbook, next work in one roadmap, and historical results in one
evidence ledger. Verification contains commands/limits rather than per-release logs.
Use immutable links for archived detail. Keep user-guide paths and original source/
test fixtures stable; check links and consumers before consolidating documents.

# Current ownership and retained compatibility

This map describes current source ownership; the external namespace retirement was merged in [PR40](https://github.com/volkswg/stock-management/pull/40). The prior Sales/Inventory, Orders/LINE, external transport and composition work is complete; all 65 files from `src/externals/` are retired. For the dated merge ledger and original evidence, see [progress](../refactoring/progress.md); for outstanding work, see the [roadmap](../refactoring/roadmap.md).

| Slice | Actual owner | Retained boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Orders | Public contracts/rules/UI; list/create/detail, mutations, attachments/images and filename rules in own application/domain; Sheets/Drive adapters; named server | Detail receives its own Shipment projection port. LINE owns draft/session coordination. No Orders→Shipments/LINE module import |
| Shipments | Public status/contracts/UI, creation/read/link/status/bill applications/ports and own Sheets/Drive adapters; server and HTTP validation helpers | Shipment→Orders uses public contracts and specifically registered gallery/projection port |
| Inventory | Contracts/quantity rules; counts/balances/reconciliation, adjustments/reversals/replacements and movements/journey primitives; own semantic adapters/server | Public HR directory and Sales dashboard readers are composed only at its server; LINE never imports Inventory persistence |
| Sales | Public report contracts, daily/dashboard/profit, sync/status/cost applications/ports, receipt IDs and Sheets projections/adapters/server | HR payroll and Inventory use the public dashboard reader; provider-native Loyverse projections stay with transport |
| Expenses | Pure Expense/Shop/Category/Input contracts, ledger/master application/ports/rules, Sheets adapter/server | HR shop reader and Sales expense projection use public contracts/entrypoints |
| HR | Pure employee/compensation/attendance/payroll/advance/settlement contracts; financial/date rules, all workforce/financial applications/ports and own persistence/runtime/hash adapters | Named workforce/payroll servers receive explicit reader ports; no legacy implementation in core, no Payroll↔Advance cycle |
| LINE workflows | Public workflow contracts/commands, sessions/context validation, order/movement journeys/replies, sequential webhook orchestration; own session adapter/runtime/server | HTTP keeps raw parsing/auth/factories/status translation; application uses semantic Orders/Inventory operations and pure shared protocol/message helpers |
| Shared Google | Root Sheets auth/JWT/client/base/row delegates/types/constants/header repair and Drive provider/factory | No feature implementation import; one persistence path |
| Shared external | Root LINE/Loyverse client/protocol/factory files; original standalone LineRichMenuClient under root LINE transport | Old constructor names/signatures/error/retry behavior remain; scripts are opt-in and never run during verification |
| Composition | `composition/google-sheets/` owns aggregate construction/factory; `hr-payroll`, `salary-advance-shops`, `employee-directory`, `orders` own compatibility wiring | May wire concrete feature adapters; feature cores never depend on composition. No DI container or alternative registry |
| Shared/runtime | Pure LINE DTO/enum/message builders and isRecord in shared; original stateful sortable ID generator in root infrastructure/runtime | No feature dependency; old helper names alias one implementation |
| Workspace/Next shell | Existing app-owned home/navigation/layout and routes | No Workspace redesign, auth/product work or unrelated UI migration |

## Physical worksheet owners

Paths below are relative to `src/modules/<owner>/infrastructure/google-sheets/`. Each class and existing header leaf have exactly one physical owner; MovementSheet has no local const.ts. The corresponding old `externals/google/sheet/sheets/` paths are retired; active imports use these physical owners. Headers retain their original mutable array identity, names and order.

| Owner / subdirectory | Class | Header export | Original default range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| orders / orders | OrdersSheet | ORDERS_SHEET_HEADERS | A:Z |
| orders / order-items | OrderItemsSheet | ORDER_ITEMS_SHEET_HEADERS | A:J |
| orders / order-bills | OrderBillsSheet | ORDER_BILLS_SHEET_HEADERS | A:G |
| shipments / shipments | ShipmentsSheet | SHIPMENTS_SHEET_HEADERS | A:M |
| shipments / shipment-orders | ShipmentOrdersSheet | SHIPMENT_ORDERS_SHEET_HEADERS | A:G |
| inventory / stock-counts | StockCountsSheet | STOCK_COUNT_HEADERS | A:I (dynamic) |
| line-workflows / user-state | UserStateSheet | USER_STATE_SHEET_HEADERS | A:H (dynamic) |
| inventory / stock-adjustments | StockAdjustmentsSheet | ADJUSTMENT_HEADERS | A:Z |
| expenses / expenses | RecordsSheet (shared constructor alias) | EXPENSE_HEADERS, CATEGORY_HEADERS, SHOP_HEADERS | A:Z |
| hr / employee-advances | PayrollRecordsSheet | ADVANCE_HEADERS, SETTLEMENT_HEADERS | A:Z |
| inventory / movements | MovementSheet | None; legacy master/detail schemas unchanged | A:N (literal) |
| hr / employees | EmployeesSheet | EMPLOYEE_HEADERS | A:I |
| hr / employee-compensations | EmployeeCompensationsSheet | EMPLOYEE_COMPENSATION_HEADERS | A:L |
| hr / employee-timesheets | EmployeeTimesheetsSheet | EMPLOYEE_TIMESHEET_HEADERS | A:G |
| sales / receipts | SalesReceiptsSheet | SALES_RECEIPT_HEADERS | A:Z |
| sales / receipt-items | SalesReceiptItemsSheet | SALES_RECEIPT_ITEM_HEADERS | A:U |
| sales / receipt-payments | SalesReceiptPaymentsSheet | SALES_RECEIPT_PAYMENT_HEADERS | A:J |
| sales / receipt-syncs | SalesReceiptSyncsSheet | SALES_RECEIPT_SYNC_HEADERS | A:I |
| sales / profit-cost-overrides | SalesProfitCostOverridesSheet | SALES_PROFIT_COST_OVERRIDE_HEADERS | A:H |

Orders A:Z is deliberately preserved rather than reduced to its current header count. Other original header-derived `lastColumnLetter(headers.length - 1)` expressions remain. Registry-created instances and canonical imports share exact class/prototype/header identity; there is no parallel registry or copied implementation. Historical test-only export projections verify the former mixed barrels against these same owners.

The six generic root Sheets declarations are GoogleSheetCellValue, GoogleSheetRow, GoogleSheetRangeUpdate, IGoogleSheet, IGoogleRowsSheet and IGoogleBatchRowsSheet. The root `service-contracts.ts` leaf retains the aggregate GoogleSheetsConfig, IGoogleSheetsService, MovementWorksheet and MovementRange plus explicit generic forwards, byte-for-byte from the retired types file. Feature classes use pure root generic types, never erased imports through the mixed aggregate index.

## Aggregate and public composition

The aggregate GoogleSheetsService still constructs the same worksheets in the same order, validates the same configuration and checks connections/batches exactly as before. All current APIs need that service shape. Its implementation/factory now live in explicit composition, outside root infrastructure; active routes use its narrow named index. It is not safe to remove or lazily split construction/health checks during this behavior-preserving refactor. There is no second registry or persistence path.

Active routes use named module servers, canonical Google/external infrastructure, composition and pure shared helpers. Their runtime graphs reach no `services`, `externals` or backend compatibility implementation. Full-service interface imports use the pure root service-contracts leaf; applications/domain never import it. Adapters still own every row/range/header/schema decision.

## Compatibility retirement gates

# Verification guide

This guide contains reproducible checks and their limits. Dated results and CI/
release evidence belong in the [single evidence ledger](progress.md), not repeated
here. A successful preview is not proof of tests, provider availability or access
control. Use existing Node 24 dependencies and `yarn.lock`; do not add a lockfile.

## Offline checks

```sh
npm test
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/migration -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

Run the relevant characterization before a behavior-sensitive move, then final
checks. Report introduced versus inherited failures and actual counts/skips.
Built-in `node:test` uses `--test-isolation=none`. Closed source loaders execute
actual owners with fake ports/auth/fetch; TypeScript transpilation is not type
checking or a security sandbox. Preserve exact allowlists, source witnesses and
historical fixtures rather than regenerating expectations to make a change pass.

## Credential-free build

Next can load `.env` files even with a cleared process environment. Prepare an
owned empty directory containing the exact reviewed source, public assets and build
configuration, existing dependencies, and only tracked `.env.example`. Inspect
filenames without printing or copying private application env files. Exclude
`.next`, caches, `.vercel`, private Git configuration and operational artifacts.

Use [`verify-build.sh`](../../tools/migration/verify-build.sh) with a real dependency
directory. On this Mac the checkout's `node_modules` is a shared symlink; its
resolved directory must be copied into the owned isolated root. Preserve the shared
install. Then, in that isolated root:

```sh
env -i PATH="$PATH" CI=1 NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 npm run build
```

For uncommitted work, copy the reviewed working files and verify their bytes;
building an archive of old HEAD does not verify those edits. Clearing credentials
is not network isolation. If prerendering gains IO, use explicit fake dependencies.
Do not run rich-menu setup, production startup, imports or real providers as checks.

## Actual PostgreSQL and historical schemas

```sh
# Fresh disposable synthetic PostgreSQL only; Docker and existing browser tools.
bash tools/migration/verify-typed-postgres.sh

# Explicit older-schema evidence with the hash-pinned PR79 record adapter.
bash tools/migration/verify-persistence-history.sh
```

The current typed verifier tests the released final schema, then the PR81 CHECK/
shared-guard artifact on independent synthetic copies. Its constraints phase is
[`verify-constraint-validation.sh`](../../tools/migration/verify-constraint-validation.sh),
**sourced by the parent**, not a standalone production command. It checks exact
51-table/15-metadata preservation, guarded refusals/atomic rollback, 23-table write
parity, all 47 timestamp fields, permissions, real application/LINE owners, native
times and browser lost-response/reload/replay. The same parent also creates a
fresh final-schema copy for `concurrent-edits.test.cjs`: actual Order/Movement
HTTP handlers, simultaneous isolated browser sessions, stale-record rejection,
child/direct-write invalidation and upload replay. Providers are forbidden.

The final parent phase also sources `verify-media-catalog.sh` on fresh final-schema
copies. It checks the guarded operator artifact and inverse, all five reference
paths, eleven catalog columns, restricted reader permissions, browser/LINE uploads,
retry/uncertainty behavior, 52-table recovery coverage and current-app operation
after rollback. It uses synthetic URLs/bytes and fake providers only.

The media phase also sources `verify-media-url-retirement.sh`. It uses new synthetic
copies for the retained URL, ID-only and column-restored layouts. Actual feature
ports, browser retry/reload, both LINE image workflows and the prior released app
exercise ID persistence, canonical URL DTOs, clearing/revision conflicts, metadata,
uncertainty/replay and rollback. Guard tests refuse missing approval, stale/wrong
target, limited readers and external dependencies; a full52-table proof excludes
only the five retired operational fields and retains import-schema evidence.

Historical verifiers intentionally use the matching older adapter and hash-bound
pre-scoped-token route/client in a disposable
credential-free tracked-source copy. `--hosted-tooling` selects the inherited
synthetic hosted-tooling campaign through that same wrapper; it is not hosted
production acceptance. Keep the pinned adapter hash, original SQL and every old
assertion. Do not introduce a production fallback to satisfy historical tests.

The GitHub [acceptance workflow](../../.github/workflows/migration-acceptance.yml)
also covers archive/recovery fingerprints, restricted backup and bundle boundaries.
Reuse passing evidence when runtime/schema code is unchanged; broaden tests when
the actual delta or a failure warrants it. Tests never authorize hosted execution.

## Compatibility and boundaries

- Use actual application, adapter and HTTP owners with fake external capabilities.
  Characterize defaults, synchronous errors, pending IO, partial failures, provider
  ordering, response loss and retries; do not mock away the behavior under test.
- Preserve money/quantity precision, nullable/empty values, Bangkok calendar rules,
  opaque IDs, stable ordering, public scalar types and LINE state/selection rules.
- Check actual flat-config lint and TypeScript-resolved runtime/type-inclusive
  graphs, browser reachability, cycles and named cross-feature public contracts.
  Keep archived inverse fixtures separate from current physical-source checks.
- Retain [`route-contracts.json`](../../tests/fixtures/route-contracts.json).
  Compare actual API/page paths and methods, response contracts and the build
  manifest; never regenerate fixtures merely to approve an accidental route change.
  Current app-paths SHA-256 is
  `32f92c7a1ef17213d7a8642ca89e3e71218984982bf1bdce66b560ef35893e1e`.
- Audit packages/env/schema/assets and browser bundles for unintended changes or
  private database strings. Follow the [architecture rules](../architecture/rules.md).

## Documentation-only changes

Verify the diff contains only intended Markdown changes. Audit every local link,
fragment, renamed path and inbound repository reference, including `AGENTS.md` and
README. Preserve original rules/invariants and map removed history to immutable
commit URLs in [progress](progress.md#historical-document-index). Historical fixture
strings and published PR bodies retain their original text; do not rewrite them.
Record the old/new file/line totals and historical URL tradeoffs. Do not create
synthetic database tests that simply mirror documentation edits.

## Limits of evidence

Offline/fake-provider results do not establish real LINE delivery, Google OAuth,
Drive uploads, Loyverse outcomes, UI visual equivalence, production concurrency,
staff authorization or recovery RTO/RPO. Distinguish local, CI, private-checkpoint
and hosted evidence in the ledger. Production read checks are not a real business
write canary. Follow the separately approved
[maintenance and recovery procedure](../database-migration.md) for live work.
